thread:
maya: Heads up — starting the quota routing schema backfill tonight 02:00 UTC. We're migrating console.metrics.route_quota -> route_quota_v2. Dualwrite will be enabled to analytics_write for 24h, then we'll run the backfill. Estimated rows: ~120M.

sam: +1. What's the plan for console reads? Will queries break if they hit inconsistent rows?

maya: We're shipping a read adapter. If route_quota_v2 row exists, read from that; else fallback to legacy. Rollout gated behind feature flag so we can flip instantly.

kevin: Dashboards — large p99 queries might scan both tables. Can we expose a unified view so Console queries don't change?

maya: Plan: create materialized view route_quota_view that does a union-select and normalizes columns via COALESCE. Backfill into route_quota_v2, refresh MV, then point Console to route_quota_view. Minimal app change.

liz: Backfill IO risk is the big one. Do we have throttling and replica-lag safeties? See playbook link: https://playbooks.internal/backfill-guides

maya: Yes — backfill runner supports rate limiting and dynamic sleep based on replica lag. Example run command: 
```bash
./backfill --table route_quota_v2 --batch 5000 --sleep-ms 100
```
We'll tune batch/sleep after first 10k rows.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: backfill-runner v1.3 -> prod at 01:50 UTC

sam: What's our rollback plan if things go sideways?

maya: If we see console p95 > 5s or errors spike, we pause runner (ctrl-c), flip feature flag to legacy_read, and let the remaining rows be processed in offline mode. We'll also cancel the MV swap. We need a reconciliation job for partial backfills.

kevin: Enforcement — will the routing policy engine read from the new table immediately? We must avoid split-brain where enforcement uses new but console shows old.

maya: Not until we switch env var ROUTE_QUOTA_TABLE -> route_quota_v2. For now both tables are readable. Enforcement stays on legacy until canary passes and we explicitly flip the env var.

liz: Can we canary by route-group? like 5% traffic to new read path?

maya: Yep. We'll add x-quota-canary header and run 5% traffic through new path for 24h. If stable, increase to 25% then 100%.

sam: Which metrics do we watch in the canary?

maya: console_p99_query_ms, console_error_rate, replica_lag_seconds, backfill_rows_processed, backfill_throughput_rps. We'll add a Grafana dashboard and alert: p95 > 2s for 10m -> pager to eng-oncall.

kevin: Also add a synthetic query probe every 30s hitting the view to catch regressions early.

liz: One more: schema change to quota_window — designers wanted timestamprange but that breaks a bunch of client code.

maya: To avoid client updates we will keep two columns: quota_window_start and quota_window_end. The materialized view will expose a timestamprange for new consumers that prefer it. DB-level compat retained.

sam: Timeline? I can help with the read adapter review.

maya: PR opened (in review). Backfill job merged. Canary + docs + dashboard by EOD. Backfill scheduled tonight 02:00 UTC. I'll ping #product when canary starts.

kevin: ack. If you need extra infra capacity for the backfill let me know (I will pretend GPUs help :stuck_out_tongue:).

sam: :thumbsup:

liz: :eyes: thanks maya

deploy-bot: Backfill-runner deploy complete to prod, tag v1.3. Logs: https://ci.internal/builds/4871
